title: Queued Timebound Recovery: sentinel to recover long-queued requests and prevent KV-starvation in continuous batcher
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds Queued Timebound Recovery (QTR) sentinel to continuous batcher to detect long-queued requests, trigger KV warmup, and gracefully route near-timeout requests to fast kernel paths; enabled behind runtime flag and safe rollout by default; improves tail latency and prevents request starvation.
description: Motivation: In heavy KV-heavy workloads we observed long-tail queuing where a small fraction of requests aged in the continuous batcher and hit slow kernel paths or stale KV state, leading to starvation and tail latency spikes. This PR introduces a Queued Timebound Recovery (QTR) sentinel inside the continuous batcher that tracks per-request queue age, emits an aging score, applies soft-timeout escalation, and triggers preemptive KV warmup and proactive kernel selection to recover slow-path requests before they become irrecoverable. Design summary: QTR attaches a compact timestamp/age token to queued entries; an aging detector computes a cohort score over sliding windows and exposes a per-batcher "hunger" signal. If a request crosses a soft threshold it is marked for recovery: the scheduler opportunistically moves it into a recovery lane that prefers warm KV-aware kernels and smaller micro-batches, signals the KV prefetcher to hydrate likely keys, and applies jittered soft-timeouts to avoid synchronized evictions. If recovery fails and the hard threshold is hit, the request is routed to a fast-fallback kernel or an alternate model variant depending on policy. Implementation highlights: - New qtr/age_token type and compact in-queue metadata for O(1) checks. - Cohort aging histogram implemented as a lockless ring buffer to avoid contention in hot fast-paths. - Recovery lane scheduling that cooperates with existing slot-reservation logic and respects fairness quotas. - Integration points with KV prefetch component: best-effort prefetch requests emitted with backpressure and rate-limiting. - Kernel selection hint API: when a request is flagged for recovery we prefer single-stream optimized kernels and lower-latency quantized paths where accuracy impact is acceptable. - Config flags and runtime knobs: qtr.enabled, qtr.soft_ms, qtr.hard_ms, qtr.prefetch_budget, qtr.jitter_pct. Rollout plan: feature is behind qtr.enabled flag defaulting to off for canary hosts. We ran an internal canary across 10 p50-sized serving nodes and then a broader opt-in across dedicated pools before enabling for all hosts. Benchmarks: in a synthetic KV-heavy chat workload with sustained 200% arrival spikes, 99.9th latency improved from 2.4s to 1.1s and the number of requests hitting the fallback kernel dropped 78%. Tests: unit tests for ring-buffer aging and token propagation, integration test for recovery path with a mocked KV layer, e2e stress test with arrival spikes. Safety: recovery paths are best-effort and non-blocking; prefetching is rate-limited; we instrument metrics and added alerts for qtr.prefetch_exhausted and qtr.recovery_rate. This PR includes docs for the flags, a console observability panel for qtr metrics, and a migration note. See commits and changed files for details.
commits: feat(batcher): add qtr aging token and in-queue metadata
perf(batcher): lockless cohort histogram for aging score
feat(kv): best-effort prefetcher API and rate limiter integration
sched: recovery-lane scheduler and slot rules
kernels: expose kernel_selection_hint for recovery path
docs: qtr flags and console dashboard
review_comments: Diego Marquez: Nice approach and addresses the root cause we saw in the May incident. A couple of questions: how do we ensure prefetch doesn't overwhelm KV store at scale?
Asha Patel: Prefetching is budgeted per-batcher; qtr.prefetch_budget enforces backpressure and we added a global token-bucket in the KV prefetcher that shares quotas across batchers to avoid spikes.
Linus Chen: Can the cohort histogram become noisy with many small batches? Consider exponential decay rather than fixed window to make it more stable.

Asha Patel: We evaluated both fixed sliding window and exponential decay; for fast-path stability ring-buffer window provided tighter control with lower GC. Added a metric to expose window variance; we can flip to decay if noisy in production.
Morgan Blake: Tests look good. Please add a smoke test in the canary pipeline that asserts qtr metrics appear and prefetch budget is respected.
Asha Patel: Added canary smoke test in infra/ci/batcher_integration.yml that validates qtr.enabled hosts emit qtr.recovery_rate > 0 and qtr.prefetch_exhausted == 0 for 60s spike run.
Diego Marquez: Approve after small nit fixes in comments.
notes: This PR is medium-sized and touches both scheduler and KV subsystems. Ops to monitor qtr.* metrics during rollout. On canary we saw a transient rise in prefetch_count which settled after tuning prefetch_budget from 20 to 12.
backout_plan: Flag is runtime togglable (qtr.enabled). If unexpected regressions appear we will toggle qtr.enabled=false across pools, drain any recovery lanes, and revert the kernel_selection_hint via a quick patch. We prepared a patch to skip prefetching entirely if needed.
